newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO DEBT OUTLOOK - Corporates hasten to market.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO DEBT OUTLOOK - Corporates hasten to market.

text.p: Mexican corporate borrowers are rushing to take advantage of positive market sentiment to refinance outstanding debt before it comes due, analysts said.
As long as pricing remains sharp, the companies should be able to keep placing debt without serious problems, they said.
"There are a lot of bonds maturing in Mexico from the middle of this year to the middle of next year," Santander Investment corporate debt analyst Jim Garvey said.
"As long as they are priced correctly, they will all go well. If they are priced too tightly, they will not go well," Garvey added.
A number of companies are nearing a foray into the market.

Railways firm Transportacin Ferroviaria Mexicana (TFM), a joint venture of Transportacin Martima Mexicana (TMM) and Kansas City Southern Industries Inc, is said to be considering a $250 million zero coupon bond and a $150 million 10-year Yankee.
The issues would replace a more expensive bridge loan, and pay down what the company owes the Mexican government for the purchase of the Northeast railroad tranche, analysts said.
Petrochemical producer Cydsa is said to be interested in placing $100 million in five- to seven-year notes in an issue led by Citibank. The proceeds could be used to refinance existing debt.

Empresas La Moderna will place a $150 million Yankee bond to reduce corporate debt, the company said recently. The company has a $150 million Eurobond, with 10.25 percent coupon, coming due in November this year.
Mexican builder Corporacin Geo is planning a $50 million, five-year Eurobond, analysts said. The issue, led by UBS and Santander could be bumped up to $75 million, MMS International said in a report.
Beverage company Femsa also has a $300 million bond coming due mid-year, and company officials have said they have worked out a $350 million three-year syndicated loan to cover that bond.
The company said it may pay off that loan through a stock offering at one of its divisions.

Among recent Mexican corporate issuers was industrial group Vitro, which this month placed $175 million notes maturing in 2002, and another series worth $250 million coming due in 2007. Those issues were bumped up from an originally planned $350 million total.
In early May, steel company Altos Hornos de Mxico (Ahmsa) also placed $425 million in Yankee bonds at five and seven years.
Among other Mexican borrowers, cement company Cemex recently obtained a $600 million, three-year revolving credit facility.
Telephone giant Telfonos de Mxico (Telmex) also said last week it received a one-year $1.0 billion loan.
